title: 2004 AMC 10B Problem 22
statement: A triangle with sides of \(5,\) \(12,\) and \(13\) has both an inscribed and a circumscribed circle. What is the distance between the centers of those circles?

solutions.text:
Since \(5^2 + 12^2 = 13^2,\) the triangle is right. Place it at \((0, 0),\) \((5, 0),\) \((0, 12).\) The circumcenter is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, \(\left(\tfrac52, 6\right).\)

The inradius satisfies \((12 - r) + (5 - r) = 13,\) so \(r = 2\) and the incenter is \((2, 2).\)

The distance is \[ \begin{gathered} \sqrt{\left(\tfrac52 - 2\right)^2 + (6 - 2)^2} \\ = \sqrt{\tfrac14 + 16} \\ = \dfrac{\sqrt{65}}{2}. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Place the right triangle with vertices \((0, 0),\) \((5, 0),\) and \((0, 12)\)
The circumcenter is the midpoint of the hypotenuse; a right triangle’s inradius is \(r = \tfrac{a + b - c}{2}\)
